survey: An open treasure chest sitting on a sandy seabed, seen from slightly above and front-right in three-quarter view. The box body shows its front face (gold-trimmed wooden planks with a keyhole plate in the centre) and its right side face, which narrows as it turns away. The plank lines on both faces run parallel to the gold top and bottom edges of each face. Gold corner feet rest flat on the sand. The curved lid is hinged along the back top edge and swung open backward. Its outer barrel faces the viewer and its right end cap shows the inside wood of the lid, which matches the camera being to the right. Coins and two gems fill the box. The coins are ellipses, flattened to match the top-down angle of the opening. One loose coin leans upright on the sand in front, and a second lies flat with a shell to the left. The camera height matches the sand: the box top, the coin pile and the flat coin all show the same downward view.
